rs11.reasoning: The apostrophe and the admiring 'Close bosom-friend... Conspiring... to load and bless' make the speaker a celebrant. Nothing in the lines is skeptical or mournful, and the speaker never narrates his own labor in the first person.
'think... will never cease' is a confident belief that the passing season will prove wrong. Nothing in the text suggests anxiety or doubt in the bees, so [1] misreads the line.

The stanza moves from Autumn as an unseen agent (stanza 1) to a personified figure an observer can find ('Thee sitting'). The farm imagery is attached to Autumn itself, so the stanza is not a general meditation on human labor.
'careless' and the hook that 'Spares the next swath' point to leisurely ease. Nothing in the text mentions toil or collapse, so [0] is unsupported.
'Steady thy laden head' stresses balanced care and a heavy load. A poverty contrast depends on outside background and goes against the 'laden' abundance.
The movement is from active 'load and bless' to 'patient look' and 'watchest' over the 'last oozings.' None of the distractors has textual support.
The stem targets line 24, 'Think not of them, thou hast thy music too,' which consoles and turns away from regret. The nostalgia belongs to line 23, not to the response.
'bloom' and 'rosy' sit beside 'soft-dying' and 'wailful... mourn,' so beauty and ending are blended. The other options are each ruled out by one side of that mix.
The lines move from ripening to fullness ('ripeness to the core') to reaped fields ('stubble-plains'), and no distractor fits.
'gathering swallows' suggests birds assembling to migrate, which hints at winter without naming it. Calling the line a 'careful record of local bird species' misdescribes what it does.
'soft-dying day' names an ending outright, and 'bloom' supplies the abundance in the same line. 'winnowing' only implies an ending indirectly, through the harvest.

The thesis tracks the poem's movement from ripening to harvest to dusk and finds beauty in both fullness and fading. The poem never says death is an illusion, and 'soft-dying' and the mourning gnats treat ending as real.

rs14.reasoning: 'Brilliantly fine', 'gold', 'white wine' set up a bright day, and the 'faint chill' is only a slight undertone. Nothing in the text says the brightness is an illusion or that the park is gloomy.
The moth-powder, the box and the nose 'of some black composition' show it is a worn object. Saying it is literally alive misreads the personification.
'Never mind' and 'when it was absolutely necessary' show she is putting it off. Nothing suggests she is anxious about other people noticing.
She blames the tingling on walking ('she supposed') and takes back 'sad' straight away, so she is explaining her feelings away, not openly admitting them.
The line follows a question and is framed as her certainty ('She was sure'). This is free indirect speech, not an objective report.
The text says the band 'didn't care how it played if there weren't any strangers present' and is 'louder and gayer' now. Nothing shows she prefers the off-season music.
'She thought' shows the praise is her own view of herself, which creates gentle irony. A tone of 'wholly admiring' ignores that qualifier.
'Wanted to shake her' is impatience, not sympathy. It shows strong feeling under her quiet listening.
Her delight in the children and the crowd ('there was always the crowd to watch') makes 'paraded' a show to watch. Nothing in the tone suggests resentment of vanity.

The bench-sitters are 'odd, silent, nearly all old', which sets them apart from the children rather than celebrating happy mingling. Her condescension is ironic because she sits there alone too. 'Disdain' is a little strong but still the best answer.

An excerpt cannot support 'for good', and the tone is fanciful. The cupboard image echoes the fur taken from its box. Minor note: the final sentence runs past line 81, but this does not affect the answer.
The retracted 'sad' and her 'sitting in other people's lives just for a minute' undercut 'wholly at peace'. The keyed thesis fits the whole passage best.
